uncertainties.note: 'that thief' (rei no dorobou-san) is an unexplained nickname not otherwise attested in the reviewed corpus checked so far; kept literal rather than guessing which character it references.

Speaker is an unnamed ally of Berkt's (unrelated to Barrel's side); no name or gender is given in the table, so none was assigned. 'Seems that one is here too' (05644) leaves the referent ('yatsu') as vague as the source.

Berkt/Barrel confrontation after Berkt's face is revealed to resemble Barrel's; speaker turns are not tagged, so lines are translated to preserve the back-and-forth without asserting which exact line belongs to which of the two beyond what character_names_021's 'keep a separate identity from Barrel even when the story connects them' note implies.

Female sentence-final particles (wa/wane) mark these as spoken by a woman, but the rows are untagged; no specific identity was inserted beyond context already evident from color()-tagged names elsewhere (e.g. 05655 'Faye', 05666 addresses 'Barrel').
The 'long-lost brothers' joke and the apology that follows are from an unnamed bystander in the post-battle scene; not assigned to a specific named crew member.

'Ensign Barrel' follows the locked rank pairing in terms_028.json (Barrel's rank shoui = Ensign); the <color(4)> span is kept around 'Barrel' only, matching the source's tag scope, with 'Ensign' placed before it per the existing 'Lieutenant Commander <color(4)>Hoshino<ce()>' rank+name convention (batch_01073).

Reordered clauses to keep <book(31)>Nergal<endbook()>, then <color(4)>Inez<ce()>, then <book(30)>Boson Jump<endbook()> in the same order the tags appear in the source line, even though natural English syntax would otherwise put Inez first.

validation.meaning_review: Independent meaning review of all 80 rows against the Japanese source (dialogue_corpus.py slice 5614 80 --context 15). Two meaning fixes applied: dialogue_05637 ('you mentioned' invented a specific prior mention not in 'rei no'/that notorious thief) and dialogue_05682 (mistranslated the shuttle explosion as the kidnapping's method instead of its cover story, contradicted by the parallel fake-death cover-up in dialogue_05684).
